title: c'è, ci sono, ecco
rule: C'è = there is; ci sono = there are. Negative with non; question by intonation. Ecco presents what is in front of you.

head: Singular
Plural
rows: Sì, ci sono. / No, non ci sono.

items.n: In the bathroom there's the washing machine.

items.t: C'è Dora? — No, non c'è. Torna alle cinque.
items.n: Is Dora in? — No, she isn't. She's back at five.
What's the matter? — Nothing, I'm tired.
items.note: che c'è? = what's up, what's wrong
a fixed phrase you will say daily

items.t: Ecco la casa. Ecco le chiavi.
items.n: Here's the flat. Here are the keys.
items.note: the same word for singular and plural

items.n: Here I am! Here he / it is! Here she / it is!

blocks.title: c'è vs è, again
blocks.text: [[C'è un bagno|There is a bathroom]] introduces something new. [[Il bagno è piccolo|The bathroom is small]] describes something known. First c'è, then è: the same order as English "there is… it is…".

items.why: Ecco stands alone, without a verb.

items.right: Ecco una moka. / C'è una moka.
items.why: "There is" in the sense of pointing is ecco; in the sense of existing, c'è.

items.q: Nel cortile ___ quattro bidoni e ___ un albero.
items.n: In the courtyard there are four bins and there's a tree.

items.why: One person, present or not: c'è / non c'è.
